additional_info.subject: ID0480358-DC/Si-D/PT-[MP/S5 170003607] fault in converter CRM:03275000101
additional_info.body:
Dear Service Coordinator / RC,
I am writing to inform that we are moving the case
0480358
﻿from the Technical Support to the eMobility RC-PT SI E Queue. We kindly ask you to take over the case and perform the necessary troubleshooting steps.
Customer:
Product:
Sicharge D - Charging Center
Main Asset:
RVP/S4170003607
Charger ID / Serial No.:
Af5yBY
Charger address/functional location:
Priority:
Medium
Handover reason: fault in converter.
Following your request and after our check. we can see that there are missing converters in DC1.
First, check the  Cancommloss  that is connected to that converter. If it is attached correctly, move to the next step.
Try swapping the converter that shows the issue with the one beside it, just to confirm whether the problem is the Cancommloss or the converter.
If the issue remains after swapping, it confirms that the converter itself is faulty. In that case, replace the converter.
Kindly pick up the case using "Pick" option in the queue or manually using the "Assign" function from the
eMobility RC-PT SI E Queue
and work on it & document the activity (Logs/Field Service Report) and attach it to the case under Documents Tab on ISP.
In case you require Expert Support, kindly create Work-order as per
unified service process
. If you need assistance with ordering Expert Support, feel free to reach out to Sousa, Afonso (SI E CS SD) at
afonso-sousa@siemens.com
or Teodoso, Rui (SI E CS SD ES) at
rui.teodoso@siemens.com
.
Kindly close the case post resolution following the case handling guidelines.
Thank you.
With best regards,
eMobility Technical Support Team –
Anass Mezzaoui

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0480358-DC/Si-D/PT-[MP/S5 170003607] fault in converter CRM:03275000101
additional_info.body:
Dear team,
Following your instructions, I confirm that all requested and recommended diagnostic procedures have been fully carried out.
The CANCommLoss connection associated with the affected converter was checked and confirmed to be correctly attached. Subsequently, the converters were swapped as instructed to identify whether the fault originated from the CANCommLoss line or from the converter itself.
After performing all tests, the fault did not follow the converter, confirming that the issue is not caused by the converter but by the CAN communication line. The detailed analysis concluded that the CAN cable/connector is damaged and must be replaced.
Please find the complete report attached for your review.
With best regards /
Mit Freundlichen Grüssen / Melhores cumprimentos
Rangel Cecconi
